heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles Hatchbox PETG natively on its stock stainless steel nozzle without needing an enclosure, achieving reliable prints at up to 167 mm/s based on a 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Thanks to the direct drive extruder and automated bed leveling, it delivers robust layer adhesion and smooth surface finishes out of the box.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVP glue stick or liquid glue as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer to prevent under-extrusion at standard layer heights.
Enable Z-Hop during retraction (0.2 mm spiral or auto z-hop) to avoid the nozzle scarring cooled PETG infill.
Configure Fan Speed Thresholds to 20% minimum and 50% maximum, keeping the auxiliary fan completely off to maintain layer bonding.
Lower First Layer Print Speed to 30 mm/s and set First Layer Bed Temperature to 78°C to secure excellent first layer adhesion without warping.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe fine stringing and nozzle whisker build-up
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and picks up atmospheric moisture, or retraction settings are insufficiently clearing the nozzle melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours; increase retraction to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s and enable wipe on loop retract (2 mm).

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Print tearing chunks out of smooth PEI sheet upon removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG creates an overly aggressive chemical bond with bare smooth PEI surfaces at standard bed temperatures.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Switch to a Textured PEI Plate and apply a thin layer of glue stick to serve as an interface and release agent, letting the plate cool completely below 35°C before removing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak interlayer adhesion and brittle vertical walls
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or printing below the optimal melt temperature for the direct-drive flow rate.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Raise nozzle temperature to 238°C-242°C, limit maximum cooling fan speed to 50%, and turn off the aux fan.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade the Bambu Lab A1 stock stainless steel nozzle for Hatchbox PETG?
faq.answer: No, Hatchbox PETG is a non-abrasive polymer, meaning the stock 0.4mm stainless steel nozzle is fully compatible and will not suffer premature wear.

faq.question: Can I print Hatchbox PETG inside an enclosure on the Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: No, the Bambu Lab A1 is designed as an open-frame printer; enclosing it can cause heat creep in the direct drive toolhead and overheat mainboard electronics.

faq.question: What is the recommended drying temperature and time for Hatchbox PETG?
faq.answer: Dry the spool at 65°C for at least 6 to 8 hours before printing, as moisture rapidly causes stringing, popping, and surface defects.

faq.question: Why is glue stick required on the PEI bed when printing PETG?
faq.answer: Unlike with PLA where glue improves bed adhesion, with PETG on PEI the glue serves as a release agent to prevent permanent bonding and surface damage to the build sheet.
